title: Job Search Hub
name: Job Search Hub
subtitle: Find, evaluate, and track jobs through Notion and the CLI.
summary: An open-source, CLI- and Notion-centered job search workflow engine. It automates multi-board job discovery, manages structured candidate facts and reusable answer banks, tracks application lifecycles, and maintains strict local data privacy.
oneLiner: Find, evaluate, and track jobs through Notion and the CLI.
description:
Job Search Hub connects job discovery, candidate qualification facts, reusable application answers, and lifecycle tracking into a single private workflow controlled through Notion and the jobhub CLI.

Key features:
• Notion-Centered Workspace: Scoped root-page discovery provisions 10 dedicated databases and numbered workflow views (1 — My search, 2 — Review jobs, 3 — Resolve questions, 4 — Apply, 5 — Track progress).
• Multi-Board Job Discovery: Automated ingestion across Greenhouse, Lever, Ashby, Recruitee, SmartRecruiters, RSS, Remotive, and manual job capture.
• Privacy & Local Security: Credentials stay in the operating system credential store (macOS Keychain) and never touch Git or Notion. Resumes and raw PDFs stay local.
• Candidate Facts & Answer Bank: Deterministic extraction from resume PDFs with human approval queue before syncing facts or reusable answers to Notion.
• Application Lifecycle Tracking: Reconciles decisions (Shortlist, Apply, Skip) and advances stages from Planned to Submitted, Interviewing, and Offer with automated timestamps and audit trails.
• Automated Scheduling & Resilient Sync: Launchd background scheduling, SQLite deduplication and rate-limiting request coordinator for Notion API limits.
story: Job search tooling often forces a false choice between closed web scrapers that hoard personal data and disjointed spreadsheets that take constant manual upkeep. I built Job Search Hub to give software engineers full ownership of their job search pipeline: the database and decision views live entirely in the user's private Notion workspace, while all document processing, API credentials, and network operations execute strictly on the local machine through a fast command-line interface.
